children.text: vande mukundamaravindadalāyatākṣaṃ kundenduśaṅkhadaśanaṃ śiśugopaveṣam
children.translated_text: I praise <s>Mukunda</s>, whose eyes are broad like lotus petals, whose teeth are like jasmine buds, the moon, and a conch, and who wears the dress of a cowherd child;

children.text: indrādidevagaṇavanditapādapīṭhaṃ vṛndāvanālayamahaṃ vasudevasūnum ||
children.translated_text: I praise the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, dwelling in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, the footstool of whose feet is adored by hosts of gods beginning with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: jayatu jayatu devo devakīnandano 'yaṃ jayatu jayatu kṛṣṇo vṛṣṇivaṃśapradīpaḥ
children.translated_text: May this god, the delight of <s>Devakī</s>, be victorious; may <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lamp of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineage, be victorious;

children.text: jayatu jayatu meghaśyāmalaḥ komalāṅgo jayatu jayatu pṛthvībhāranāśo mukundaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Mukunda</s>, dark as a cloud, soft-limbed, the destroyer of earth's burden, be victorious, victorious.

children.text: mukunda mūrdhnā praṇipatya yāce bhavantamekāntamiyantamartham
children.translated_text: O <s>Mukunda</s>, bowing with my head, I ask from you only this single favor:

children.text: avismṛtistvaccaraṇāravinde bhave bhave me 'sti bhavatprasādāt ||
children.translated_text: by your grace, may I have unfailing remembrance of your lotus feet in birth after birth.

children.text: śrīmukundapadāmbhojamadhunaḥ paramādbhutam
children.translated_text: The honey of the lotus of glorious <s>Mukunda</s>'s feet is supremely wondrous;

children.text: yatpāyino na muhyanti muhyanti yadapāyinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who drink it are not deluded, while those who fail to drink it are deluded.

children.text: nāhaṃ vande tava caraṇayordvandvamadvandvahetoḥ kumbhīpākaṃ gurumapi hare nārakaṃ nāpanetum
children.translated_text: I do not worship the pair of your feet, O <s>Hari</s>, as a means to freedom from duality, nor to remove even the terrible hell called <s>Kumbhīpāka</s>;

children.text: ramyā rāmā mṛdutanulatā nandane nāpi rantuṃ bhāve bhāve hṛdayabhavane bhāvaye 'haṃ bhavantam ||
children.translated_text: nor to sport in <s>Nandana</s> with lovely women whose bodies are tender creepers. In existence after existence, in the house of my heart, I contemplate you.

children.text: nāsthā dharme na vasunicaye naiva kāmopabhoge yadbhāvyaṃ tadbhavatu bhagavanpūrvakarmānurūpam
children.translated_text: I have no attachment to <s>dharma</s> (religious duty), nor to heaps of wealth, nor indeed to the enjoyment of desire. Let whatever must happen, O Lord, happen according to previous karma.

children.text: etatprārthyaṃ mama bahumataṃ janmajanmāntare 'pi tvatpādāmbhoruhayugagatā niścalā bhaktirastu ||
children.translated_text: This alone is my prayer, and it is highly cherished by me: even through birth after birth, may there be unwavering devotion fixed on the pair of lotuses that are your feet.

children.text: divi vā bhuvi vā mamāstu vāso narake vā narakāntake prakāmam
children.translated_text: Whether my dwelling be in heaven, on earth, or even in hell, O destroyer of hell, as you please,

children.text: avadhīritaśāradāravindau caraṇau te maraṇe 'pi cintayāmi ||
children.translated_text: even at death I contemplate your feet, which put to shame the autumn lotus.

children.text: sarasijanayane saśaṅkhacakre murabhidi mā virameha citta rantum
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one, bearing conch and discus, slayer of <s>Mura</s>, may my mind not cease to delight here;

children.text: sukhakaramaparaṃ na jātu jāne haricaraṇasmaraṇāmṛtena tulyam ||
children.translated_text: I know no other thing that brings happiness equal to the nectar of remembering <s>Hari</s>'s feet.

children.text: mā bhairmandamano vicintya bahudhā yāmīściraṃ yātanā nāmī naḥ prabhavanti pāparipavaḥ svāmī nanu śrīdharaḥ
children.translated_text: Do not be afraid, dull mind, thinking in many ways of the long torments of <s>Yama</s>; these enemy-sins have no power over us, for surely <s>Śrīdhara</s> is our master.

children.text: ālasyaṃ vyapanīya bhaktisulabhaṃ dhyāyasva nārāyaṇaṃ lokasya vyasanāpanodanakaro dāsasya kiṃ na kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cast off laziness and meditate on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, easily reached by devotion. He removes the distress of the world; what would he not be able to do for his servant?

children.text: bhavajaladhimagādhaṃ dustaraṃ nistareyaṃ kathamahamiti ceto mā sma gāḥ kātaratvam
children.translated_text: O mind, do not fall into timidity, thinking, 'How shall I cross the deep and hard-to-cross ocean of becoming?'

children.text: sarasijadṛśi deve tāvakī bhaktirekā narakabhidi niṣaṇṇā tārayiṣyatyavaśyam ||
children.translated_text: Your one devotion, fixed on the lotus-eyed god, the destroyer of hell, will certainly carry you across.

children.text: tṛṣṇātoye madanapavanoddhūtamohormimāle dārāvarte sahajatanayagrāhasaṃghākule ca
children.translated_text: In the great ocean called <s>saṃsāra</s>, with craving as its water, with rows of delusion-waves stirred up by the wind of passion, with wives as whirlpools, and crowded with swarms of sharks in the form of natural-born sons,

children.text: saṃsārākhye mahati jaladhau majjatāṃ nastridhāmanpādāmbhoje varada bhavato bhaktināve prasīda ||
children.translated_text: while we are sinking, O threefold-abode, O boon-giver, be gracious: may the boat of devotion to your lotus feet save us.

children.text: pṛthvīreṇuraṇuḥ payāṃsi kaṇikāḥ phalguḥ sphuliṅgo laghustejo niḥśvasanaṃ maruttanutaraṃ randhraṃ susūkṣmaṃ nabhaḥ
children.translated_text: The dust of the earth is but an atom; the waters are drops; fire is a feeble, tiny spark; wind is a slight breath, still thinner; and space is a very subtle opening;

children.text: kṣudrā rudrapitāmahaprabhṛtayaḥ kīṭāḥ samastāḥ surā dṛṣṭe yatra sa tāvako vijayate bhūmāvadhūtāvadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: where you are seen, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s>, and the others are small, and all the gods are insects. Your greatness there triumphs, its limit cast down upon the earth.

children.text: āmnāyābhyasanānyaraṇyaruditaṃ kṛcchravratānyanvahaṃ medaśchedapadāni pūrtavidhayaḥ sarve hutaṃ bhasmani
children.translated_text: Study of the Vedas is crying in the wilderness; severe vows performed day after day are merely steps toward cutting flesh; works of public merit are all oblations into ashes;

children.text: tīrthānāmavagāhanāni ca gajasnānaṃ vinā yatpadadvandvāmbhoruhasaṃstutiṃ vijayate devaḥ sa nārāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and bathing in holy places is an elephant's bath, without praise of the lotus pair of his feet. Victorious is that god, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: ānanda govinda mukunda rāma nārāyaṇānanta nirāmayeti
children.translated_text: '<s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, endless one, free from disease'--

children.text: vaktuṃ samartho 'pi na vakti kaścidaho janānāṃ vyasanāni mokṣe ||
children.translated_text: though someone is able to say this, he does not say it. Alas, the misfortunes of people regarding liberation!

children.text: kṣīrasāgarataraṅgaśīkarāsāratārakitacārumūrtaye
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Mādhava</s>, enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, whose lovely form is starred by the spray from waves of the milk ocean,

children.text: bhogibhogaśayanīyaśāyine mādhavāya madhuvidviṣe namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who lies upon a couch made from the coils of the serpent.

children.text: vātsalyādabhayapradānasamayādārtārtinirvāpaṇādaudāryādaghaśoṣaṇādagaṇitaśreyaḥpadaprāpaṇāt
children.translated_text: Because of his affection, because he grants fearlessness at the proper time, because he extinguishes the suffering of the afflicted, because of his generosity, because he dries up sin, and because he gives access to incalculable states of welfare,

children.text: sevyaḥ śrīpatireva sarvajagatāmekāntataḥ sākṣiṇaḥ prahlādaśca vibhīṣaṇaśca karirāṭ pāñcālyahalyā dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīpati</s> alone is to be served single-mindedly by the whole world. <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the king of elephants, <s>Pāñcālī</s>, <s>Ahalyā</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s> are witnesses.

children.text: nāthe śrīpuruṣottame trijagatāmekādhipe cetasā sevye svasya padasya dātari pare nārāyaṇe tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: When the lord <s>Śrīpuruṣottama</s>, the sole ruler of the three worlds, the supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, giver of his own station, stands ready to be served by the mind,

children.text: yaṃ kaṃcitpuruṣādhamaṃ katipayagrāmeśamalpādarthadaṃ sevāyai mṛgayāmahe naramaho mūḍhā varākā vayam ||
children.translated_text: alas, we foolish wretches seek out some lowest man, a petty village lord who gives only a little wealth, in order to serve him.

children.text: bho lokāḥ śṛṇuta prasūtimaraṇavyādheścikitsāmimāṃ yogajñāḥ samudāharanti munayo yāṃ yājñavalkyādayaḥ
children.translated_text: O people, listen to this cure for the disease of birth, death, and sickness, which sages skilled in yoga, such as <s>Yājñavalkya</s> and the others, proclaim:

children.text: antarjyotirameyamekamamṛtaṃ kṛṣṇākhyamāpīyatāṃ yatpītaṃ paramauṣadhaṃ vitanute nirvāṇamātyantikam ||
children.translated_text: drink the inner light, immeasurable, one, immortal, called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; when drunk, that supreme medicine produces final liberation.

children.text: baddhenāñjalinā natena śirasā gātraiḥ saromodgamaiḥ kaṇṭhena savaragadgadena nayanenodgīrṇabāṣpāmbunā
children.translated_text: With hands joined, head bowed, limbs thrilled with horripilation, throat choked and stammering with emotion, and eyes pouring out tears,

children.text: nityaṃ tvaccaraṇāravindayugaladhyānāmṛtāsvādinām asmākaṃ sarasīruhākṣa satataṃ saṃpadyatāṃ jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one, may our life always come to pass in the constant tasting of the nectar of meditation on the pair of lotuses that are your feet.

children.text: tattvaṃ bruvāṇāni paraṃ parasmādaho kṣarantīva sudhāṃ padāni
children.translated_text: Ah, words that speak the truth beyond the supreme seem to pour forth nectar.

children.text: āvartaya prāñjalirasmi jihve nāmāni nārāyaṇagocarāṇi ||
children.translated_text: O tongue, repeat, for I stand with joined hands, the names whose object is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: idaṃ śarīraṃ pariṇāmapeśalaṃ patatyavaśyaṃ ślathasaṃdhi jarjaram
children.translated_text: This body, skillful only in decay, will certainly fall, its joints loosened and worn out.

children.text: kimauṣadhaiḥ kliśyasi mūḍha durmate nirāmayaṃ kṛṣṇarasāyanaṃ piba ||
children.translated_text: Why do you torment yourself with medicines, foolish and misguided one? Drink the disease-free elixir of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: śrīmannāma procya nārāyaṇākhyaṃ yena prāptā vāñchitaṃ pāpino 'pi
children.translated_text: By uttering the blessed name called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, even sinners have obtained what they desired.

children.text: hā naḥ pūrvaṃ vākpravṛttā na tasmiṃstena prāptaṃ garbhavāsādiduḥkham ||
children.translated_text: Alas, our speech did not engage in that before; therefore we have obtained the suffering beginning with dwelling in the womb.

children.text: mā drākṣaṃ kṣīṇapuṇyānkṣaṇamapi bhavato bhaktihīnānpadābje mā śrauṣaṃ śravyabaddhaṃ tava caritamapāsyānyadākhyānajātam
children.translated_text: May I not behold, even for a moment, those whose merit is exhausted and who are without <s>bhakti</s> at your lotus feet; may I not hear any mass of other tales, bound for hearing, after setting aside your deeds.

children.text: mā sprākṣaṃ mādhava tvāmapi bhuvanapate cetasāpahnuvānaṃ mā bhūvaṃ tvatsaparyāvyatikararahito janmajanmāntare 'pi ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, O lord of the worlds, may I not touch one who denies even you in his mind; even in birth after birth, may I not be without the activity of worshipping you.

children.text: madana parihara sthitiṃ madīye manasi mukundapadāravindadhāmni
children.translated_text: O <s>Madana</s>, abandon your station in my mind, which is the abode of the lotus feet of <s>Mukunda</s>.

children.text: haranayanakṛśānunā kṛśo 'si smarasi na cakraparākramaṃ murāreḥ ||
children.translated_text: You have been made thin by the fire of <s>Hara</s>'s eye; do you not remember the valor of <s>Murāri</s>'s discus?

children.text: dārā vārākaravarasutā te 'ṅgajo 'yaṃ viriñcaḥ stotā vedastava suragaṇo bhṛtyavargaḥ prasādaḥ
children.translated_text: Your wife is the daughter of the ocean, your son here is <s>Viriñca</s>; the Veda is your praiser, the host of gods is your class of servants, and grace is yours.

children.text: muktirmadhye jagadavikalaṃ tāvake devakī te mātā mitraṃ balaripusutastattvato 'nyanna jāne ||
children.translated_text: Liberation is in your midst, the whole world is yours, <s>Devakī</s> is your mother, and the son of <s>Balaripu</s> is your friend; in truth I know nothing else.

children.text: jihve kīrtaya keśavaṃ muraripuṃ ceto bhaja śrīdharaṃ pāṇidvandva samarcayācyutakathāṃ śrotradvaya tvaṃ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: O tongue, praise <s>Keśava</s>, the foe of <s>Mura</s>; O mind, worship <s>Śrīdhara</s>; O pair of hands, worship him; O pair of ears, hear the story of <s>Acyuta</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ lokaya locanadvaya harergacchāṅghriyugmālayaṃ jighra ghrāṇa mukundapādatulasīṃ mūrdhannamādhokṣajam ||
children.translated_text: O pair of eyes, behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; go to the abode of <s>Hari</s>'s two feet. O nose, smell the tulasī from <s>Mukunda</s>'s feet; O head, bow to <s>Adhokṣaja</s>.

children.text: yatkṛṣṇapraṇipātadhūlidhavalaṃ tadvai śiraḥ syācchubhaṃ te netre tamasojjhite surucire yābhyāṃ harirdṛśyate
children.translated_text: That head which is whitened by the dust from bowing to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed auspicious; those two eyes by which <s>Hari</s> is seen are beautiful, freed from darkness.

children.text: sā buddhirniyamairyamaiśca vimalā yā mādhavadhyāyinī sā jihvāmṛtavarṣiṇī pratipadaṃ yā stauti nārāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: That intellect is stainless through restraints and observances which meditates on <s>Mādhava</s>; that tongue showers nectar which praises <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at every step.

children.text: bhaktadveṣibhujaṃgagāruḍamaṇis trailokyarakṣāmaṇirgopīlocanacātakāmbudamaṇiḥ saundaryamudrāmaṇiḥ
children.translated_text: May the crest-jewel <s>Gopāla</s> point out our highest good: the Garuḍa-jewel against the serpent-arms of those who hate devotees, the jewel protecting the three worlds, the raincloud-jewel for the cātaka-birds that are the gopīs' eyes, the seal-jewel of beauty,

children.text: śrīkāntāmaṇirukmiṇīghanakucadvandvaikabhūṣāmaṇiḥ śreyo dhyeyaśikhām nirdiśatu no gopālacūḍāmaṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the jewel of <s>Śrīkāntā</s>, the single ornament-jewel for the two firm breasts of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, the crest-jewel to be meditated upon for blessedness.

children.text: śatruchedaikamantraṃ sakalamupaniṣadvākyasaṃpūjyamantraṃ saṃsārottāramantraṃ samuditamanasāṃ saṅganiryāṇamantram
children.translated_text: The one mantra for cutting down enemies, the mantra honored by all the sentences of the Upaniṣads, the mantra that carries one across saṃsāra, the mantra that releases those whose minds are gathered from attachment,

children.text: sarvaiśvaryaikamantraṃ vyasanabhujagasaṃdaṣṭasaṃtrāṇamantraṃ jihve śrīkṛṣṇamantraṃ japa japa satataṃ janmasāphalyamantram ||
children.translated_text: the one mantra for all sovereignty, the mantra that rescues those bitten by the serpent of misfortune: O tongue, chant, chant always the mantra '<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>,' the mantra that makes birth fruitful.

children.text: vyāmohoddalanauṣadhaṃ munimanovṛttipravṛttyauṣadhaṃ daityānarthakarauṣadhaṃ trijagatāṃ saṃjīvanaikauṣadham
children.translated_text: The medicine that uproots delusion, the medicine that sets in motion the tendencies of sages' minds, the medicine that brings ruin to demons, the sole life-giving medicine for the three worlds,

children.text: bhaktārtipraśamauṣadhaṃ bhavabhayapradhvaṃsi divyauṣadhaṃ śreyaḥprāptikarauṣadhaṃ piba manaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanāmauṣadham ||
children.translated_text: the medicine that pacifies the suffering of devotees, the divine medicine that destroys the fear of becoming, the medicine that brings the attainment of blessedness: O mind, drink the medicine of the name of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: āścaryametaddhi manuṣyaloke sudhāṃ parityajya viṣaṃ pibanti
children.translated_text: This is indeed astonishing in the human world: people abandon nectar and drink poison.

children.text: nāmāni nārāyaṇagocarāṇi tyaktvānyavācaḥ kuhakāḥ paṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Tricksters, having given up the names whose object is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, recite other words.

children.text: lāṭīnetrapuṭīpayodharaghaṭīrevātaṭīduṣkuṭīpāṭīradrumavarṇanena kavibhirmūḍhairdinaṃ nīyate
children.translated_text: Foolish poets spend the day describing the corners of eyes, cups of breasts, banks of the <s>Revā</s>, wretched huts, and pāṭīra trees.

children.text: govindeti janārdaneti jagatāṃ nātheti kṛṣṇeti ca vyāhāraiḥ samayastadekamanasāṃ puṃsāmatikrāmati ||
children.translated_text: But for men whose minds are fixed on that one, time passes with utterances such as '<s>Govinda</s>,' '<s>Janārdana</s>,' 'lord of the worlds,' and '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'.

children.text: ayācyamakreyamayātayāmamapācyamakṣayyamadurbharaṃ me
children.translated_text: Not to be begged for, not to be bought, not stale, not to be cooked, inexhaustible, and not hard for me to carry,

children.text: astyeva pātheyamitaḥ prayāṇe śrīkṛṣṇanāmamṛtabhāgadheyam ||
children.translated_text: there surely exists provision for my journey from here: the fortunate share of the nectar of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s name.

children.text: yasya priyau śrutadharau kavilokagītau mitre dvijanmaparivāraśivāvabhūtām
children.translated_text: His two dear friends were learned in scripture and sung by the world of poets, and they became auspicious attendants among the twice-born.

children.text: tenāmbujākṣacaraṇāmbujaṣaṭpadena rājñā kṛtā stutiriyaṃ kulaśekhareṇa ||
children.translated_text: By that king <s>Kulaśekhara</s>, a bee at the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed one, this hymn was composed.
